title: Execution Requirement Readiness
description: Experimental (`media_buy.execution_readiness`). Whether the caller's account can satisfy one entry of a product's `execution_requirements[]`. Account-scoped: it appears only in the response-level `execution_readiness` map and MUST NOT be disclosed across accounts. Advisory: `create_media_buy` revalidates, and an unmet requirement still fails per `error-details/execution-requirement-unmet.json` or `AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED`.

requirement.description: The product's declared requirement, echoed. MUST deep-equal an entry of that product's current `execution_requirements[]`. The map is versioned separately from the product feed, so a buyer whose cached product has no matching entry has a stale feed and SHOULD refetch it.

status.description: Readiness of this requirement. For `downstream_connection`, derived from `connection_state.status`: `connected` and `not_required` are `ready`; `missing`, `pending`, `expired`, and `revoked` are `setup_required`; `unknown` is `unknown`. `selection_required` and `input_required` apply only to `event_source` and `catalog`, the kinds with a request binding.

binding_field.description: Where the buyer binds the chosen resource, in the JSONPath-lite form of `error.field`: `packages[].optimization_goals[].event_sources[].event_source_id` for `event_source`, `packages[].catalogs[]` for `catalog`. Omitted for `downstream_connection`, which is satisfied by completing the connection. For `event_source` and `catalog`, SHOULD be present when `status` is `ready` or `selection_required`.

resolved.description: The resource to use when `status` is `ready`, for `event_source` and `catalog`. REQUIRED then. For these kinds the buyer MUST still bind `resource_id`: `ready` is not permission to omit the binding, and an unbound requirement is `not_bound` per `error-details/execution-requirement-unmet.json`.

resource_id.description: Directly usable in `binding_field`: the `event_source_id` as returned by `sync_event_sources` (including a seller-managed source), or a `catalog_id` that `packages[].catalogs[]` accepts. Not a raw platform ID unless that is the ID the binding field accepts.

name.description: Human-readable name of the resource on the seller's platform.

candidates.description: Suitable resources the account has, when `status` is `selection_required`, for `event_source` and `catalog`. Account-scoped; never disclosed across accounts. Lists resources the seller has no evidence would fail the requirement; it MAY include a resource whose event types or catalog type it cannot verify.

name.description: Human-readable name of the resource on the seller's platform.

connection_state.description: For `downstream_connection`: the account's state for the connection the seller would use (its documented default when several are connected). REQUIRED for that kind, with `status`. When `missing`, `expired`, or `revoked` it SHOULD carry `authorization_url` or `authorization_instructions`; `pending` MAY omit both. `resource_ref` and `connection_id` MAY be present only when safe to disclose to this account. Not used for other kinds.

unknown_reason.description: Why the seller could not check. REQUIRED when `status` is `unknown`. `permission_denied`: the seller's credential for the account cannot read this resource kind. `platform_unavailable`: the platform read failed or timed out. `not_evaluated`: the seller skipped it, for example past its evaluation budget.

issues.description: Actionable detail for a non-`ready` status: what is missing, which resources were ineligible and why, or what failed. Sellers SHOULD limit this to the 3-5 most actionable items.
